title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Refunding a Payer After an Upheld Post-Payment Denial of Outpatient Surgery
content:
**Standing rule (Credit Balance & Recovery).** When a payer has denied, after paying it, the services on a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim for an Outpatient Surgery Account, and Riverbend's own provider-level appeal of that denial has been decided against it (the claim is in denied status and at least one appeal is filed on it), Riverbend refunds to the payer the payment attributable to the services the denial reached and records the refund as one payer recovery entry on the claim with the reason code WO-72; any other claim gets nothing here.

The Outpatient Surgery Account is the patient class of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) the claim bills. The payer classes in scope are the Commercial PPO Claim, Commercial HMO Claim and Marketplace Exchange Plan Claim classes of the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing).

**How the recovery is recorded.** For a refund Riverbend records under this rule or under its rule for observation and emergency claims, and only for such a refund, the recovery re-opens the amount expected from the payer by the amount refunded and is recorded against the remittance that carried the refunded payment (the claim's earliest-posted payer payment; when several payer payments share that earliest posting date, the one whose remittance trace number comes first in alphabetical order), with that remittance's trace number and date; every other payer takeback re-opens the amount expected from the payer by the amount recovered and is recorded against the remittance that carried it.

| Claim state | Result under this rule |
|---|---|
| In-scope payer class, Outpatient Surgery Account, denied status, at least one appeal filed | one payer recovery entry, reason code WO-72 |
| Any other combination | nothing is recorded under this rule |

## Recording the refund: `refund_surgery_claim_payment_239964f7`
**Capability.** Books, on one insurance claim, the payer's recovery of a payment it made on the claim, refunded to the payer by Riverbend: one payer recovery entry with the reason code WO-72, recorded against the payer remittance that carried the claim's payer payment with the smallest posting date (equal dates: the smallest remittance trace number), with that remittance's trace number and date copied onto the entry. The entry is dated today and raises the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. What the patient owes does not change, and the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `refund_surgery_claim_payment_239964f7` and then calls it.

**Parameters**
| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` | the reference number of the insurance claim whose payment the payer is recovering, as shown by the claim lookup for the patient | identifier |
| `amount_usd` | the amount refunded to the payer | USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent by the caller; posted exactly as given |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Recovery <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason code WO-72, against remittance <remit_trace_number>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The entry reference identifies the new claim activity entry; the remittance trace number is that of the remittance carrying the earliest-posted payer payment (empty when the claim has no payment); the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer, in USD with 2 decimal places. The receipt appearing is the success signal.
